definitions.explanation: A trip taken by a group, especially a school outing to a nearby destination.
A recreational outdoor trip, often involving walking.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠足|えんそく}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
{遠足|えんそく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made a lunch box for the school trip.

examples.english: The children are really looking forward to the school trip.

examples.english: I went on a hike with friends on the weekend and ate a packed lunch.
When spring comes, I get the urge to go outside like going on an outing.

notes:
USAGE: {遠足|えんそく} typically refers to school excursions for elementary and middle school students, but can also mean hiking trips.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{遠足|えんそく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ (to go on an excursion)
・{遠足|えんそく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ (excursion day)
・{遠足|えんそく}⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧ (excursion mood - feeling excited)

SCHOOL CONTEXT: Japanese schools often organize {遠足|えんそく} in spring and autumn to parks, zoos, or historical sites.

CULTURAL NOTE: {遠足|えんそく} evokes childhood memories and is associated with ⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧ (packed lunch) and ⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧ (snacks) that children bring.
